newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms, interbank rate higher late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms, interbank rate higher late.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed against the dollar on late selling of the U.S. unit, dealers said on Friday.

The baht rallied to 25.905/25.915 near the close from 25.930/25.940 at midday and 25.965/25.975 early in the morning. Dealers, however, did not see clear signs of central bank intervention to shore up the baht.
"There was heavy dollar selling in late afternoon. As we know, it was not a result of central bank intervention," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
Dealers said offshore players squared dollar positions ahead of the weekend following their heavy dollar buying this week.
"High short-term baht interest rates also attracted market interest in the baht," the dealer said.
The central bank intervened in offshore markets twice on Thursday to help stabilise the baht against the dollar.
The baht's latest selloff was partly triggered by negative market reaction to monthly economic figures released by the Bank of Thailand on Thursday.
A high December balance of payments deficit and a hefty government budget deficit during the October/December quarter fuelled increasing concern about a weaker Thai economic outlook, dealers said.
The baht/dollar mid-rate stood unchanged at 25.87.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 14.50-15.00 percent near the close from 15.00-17.00 before noon and 13.50-14.00 in the morning amid tight liquidity, dealers said.

"The interbank rate is likely to rise further on Monday. Some banks will need funds to settle dollar buying this week," a currency dealer said. Higher fund demand ahead of the Lunar New Year will curb money supply next week, dealers said.
The one-month baht/dollar premium fell to 11.50/12.50 satangs per dollar from 13.00/14.00 in the morning.
